# Melbourne girl Leah Halton officially has the most liked TikTok of all time with 73 million likes

Content creator Leah Halton has thanked her followers after setting an “incredible milestone” thanks to a 12 second video she posted to the social media platform.

Listen to this article

2 min

X

There are 73 million reasons why Melbourne girl Leah Halton can boast an admirable claim to fame.

Two years after blowing up TikTok with a 12 second lip synching clip, Halton’s video is now the most liked of all time on the platform.

She’s clocked over 73 million likes on the miming to Praise Jah in the Moonlight by YG Marley, eclipsing the previous most liked lip synching video of Bella Poarch.

> @looooooooch Summer😊#Inverted♬ Praise Jah In The Moonlight - YG Marley

Leah Halton’s video is now the most liked of all time on TikTok.

Halton’s video has clocked over 73 million likes.

Her viral 12 second lip synching clip was posted two years ago.

“Today is a very exciting day because we just broke the record for the most liked TikTok of all time,’’ Halton said on TikTok on Monday.

“I said we because I couldn’t have done this without any of you guys. I’m feeling so excited and so blessed. It’s actually crazy because this time two years ago I posted the viral video and this time last year it hit a billion views and then this time this year, it became the most liked video on TikTok. It’s just crazy, is February my month?”

Halton spoke about the “incredible milestone” while she did her make up, continuing with an Oscars worthy speech.

# Leah Halton’s Viral TikTok Breaks the All‑Time Likes Record

- February 13, 2026
- Business

Australian TikTok creator Leah Halton has made history with her viral lip-sync video to YG Marley’s Praise Jah in the Moonlight, setting a new milestone as the most liked video on the platform. As of early 2026, Halton’s post has surpassed 74 million likes, overtaking Bella Poarch’s previous record for her viral “M to the B” lip-sync video, which held the title for a long time.

This achievement not only marks a personal victory for Halton but also underscores the growing influence of short-form video content and how TikTok has become a primary stage for creators to reach massive audiences. Halton’s success illustrates the way the app’s algorithm promotes content that resonates deeply with users, propelling creators into the spotlight through viral engagement.

TikTok’s ability to elevate creators to global recognition continues to grow, and Halton’s record-breaking success serves as an example of the platform’s power in shaping online culture and entertainment. Her video has captured attention across multiple social media platforms, leading to widespread recognition of her achievement.

## The Video That Struck a Chord with Viewers

Halton’s viral video resonated with millions due to its relatable and authentic feel. Unlike heavily produced content, the video’s casual setting—where Halton lip-syncs while sitting in her car—highlighted its natural, down-to-earth appeal. The simplicity of the clip allowed viewers to connect with Halton in an unfiltered way, offering an alternative to the more polished and choreographed content often seen on the platform.

The song choice also played a role in the video’s viral success. Praise Jah in the Moonlight was already gaining popularity on TikTok when Halton posted the video, which helped propel the track to even greater visibility. The combination of music and authenticity made it stand out among the usual viral content, drawing in a diverse audience.

What sets Halton’s video apart from others is its genuine and approachable vibe, which contrasts with the often highly curated nature of TikTok content. This authenticity, paired with the song’s rising popularity, created the perfect storm for a viral success story. It’s a clear example of how TikTok users are increasingly drawn to relatable content that feels genuine and uncontrived.

## The Power of TikTok’s Algorithm and Growing Engagement

TikTok’s algorithm has played a significant role in Halton’s success, as it amplifies content that resonates with large numbers of users. While early TikTok trends often involved highly choreographed dances and comedic skits, more recent viral content shows that authenticity and emotional resonance have taken precedence. The rise of casual, unpolished clips like Halton’s reflects how TikTok has shifted from entertainment-focused videos to content that reflects personal expression and relatability.

Halton’s post demonstrates how the platform’s algorithm can propel even simple content into widespread fame, as long as it aligns with what viewers are currently interested in. As TikTok continues to evolve, the increasing importance of relatability over spectacle is becoming a defining characteristic of what resonates with audiences. The success of her video is a testament to the way TikTok’s system amplifies content that feels personal and accessible to users, leading to greater engagement and connection with creators.

The platform’s dynamic algorithm, which prioritizes videos that keep users engaged, allowed Halton’s video to break out and gain visibility across the globe. TikTok’s continuous push to refine its ability to detect and promote viral content helped this video reach new heights, making it a defining moment for both Halton and TikTok as a platform.

## The Global Reaction to Halton’s Milestone

Halton’s achievement has sparked a global conversation, with fans and creators alike expressing their admiration for the record-breaking moment. Messages of congratulations poured in across TikTok, Instagram, and Twitter, as creators and viewers shared their excitement and praised Halton for her success. Her record has been covered widely in mainstream media, with outlets discussing the significance of her achievement in the context of TikTok’s evolving role in entertainment.

Her success is also seen as a symbol of how TikTok continues to shape trends in global culture. Halton, who was previously known primarily for her lifestyle and influencer content, has now become a central figure in the conversation about TikTok’s ability to elevate creators into the global spotlight. The engagement on her video shows the powerful impact TikTok has on how content is shared and consumed worldwide, with millions of viewers celebrating her moment of success.

Not only has the video garnered millions of views, but it has also captured the collective attention of various communities, from TikTok enthusiasts to mainstream media outlets. This reaction highlights the growing influence of individual creators on digital platforms and their ability to inspire wide-reaching conversations across multiple audiences.

## Australian Creators Making Their Mark on TikTok

Halton’s viral success reflects a larger trend of Australian creators gaining significant influence on TikTok. Creators from Australia have been making waves globally, with several rising stars reaching audiences in diverse regions. Halton’s achievement marks an important moment for Australian influencers, showcasing their ability to impact the global digital space.

This trend of Australian creators finding success on TikTok highlights the global nature of the platform and how creators from various regions can connect with audiences around the world. Halton’s story adds to a growing list of Australian creators who have made their mark, whether through viral content or by building dedicated followings.

TikTok has provided a platform where creators from different backgrounds and regions can reach large, engaged audiences. Halton’s success, in particular, demonstrates the increasing global diversity of TikTok creators and the way audiences are embracing voices from all parts of the world.

## TikTok’s Evolving Role in Shaping Entertainment

Halton’s record-breaking video illustrates how TikTok continues to redefine what it means to go viral and gain cultural recognition. The platform’s ability to turn casual creators into global influencers has fundamentally changed the landscape of digital entertainment. TikTok’s influence extends beyond individual creators, as it continues to reshape how content is consumed, produced, and shared.

Halton’s viral moment also signals a larger trend within the platform, where authenticity and simplicity now carry as much weight as highly produced content. As TikTok’s algorithm prioritizes content that resonates with audiences on a deeper, more personal level, creators have more opportunities to share relatable, raw, and genuine expressions with a wider community. This shift is helping to further shape TikTok’s evolution into a platform for personal connection and expression, rather than solely entertainment.

With millions of new users joining TikTok each month, the platform’s influence over entertainment and digital culture is expected to grow. The success of videos like Halton’s showcases how everyday moments can now have a global impact, redefining the way social media is used for personal expression and public connection.

# Most popular TikTok of all-time soundtracked by Blackpool grime song

The video, from Hawaii-based Bella Poarch, has racked up over 30 million likes

By Will Richards

14th September 2020

TikTok - Credit: Alamy

A TikTok video soundtracked by a Blackpool grime song has become the most popular video on the entire platform.

The Blackpool grime scene has risen to prominence since the release of a 2016 documentary about the emerging genre.

A follow-up documentary was then released a year later, which focused largely on a beef between Blackpool grime MCs Soph Aspin and MC Millie B, the latter of which recorded a diss track called ‘Soph Aspin Send’, also known as ‘M To The B’.

A new video on TikTok has now gone viral, collecting over 32 million likes and becoming the most popular video on the entire site.

The video sees 19-year-old Bella Poarch from Hawaii reacting to ‘Soph Aspin Send’ while using the platform’s Face Zoom filter. It went viral shortly after it was posted in mid-August, and a number of celebrities then impersonated Poarch’s video, leading its view count to grow even further.

Watch the clip below:

This week, TikTok announced it had rejected a bid from Microsoft to manage its US operations, instead choosing Oracle to take over the company in the States.

Microsoft, which was in talks to purchase TikTok’s American arm, announced yesterday (September 13) that its proposal was declined.

In August, President Donald Trump threatened to ban TikTok by tomorrow (September 15) if it wasn’t sold off to an American company, on the grounds that it was a threat to national security in the US due to its Chinese ownership.

A few weeks later, TikTok announced it was suing the President, saying it had “no choice but to take action to protect our rights.”

Who Has the Most Likes on TikTok in 2026? The Complete Creator Rankings

Charli D'Amelio holds the title of who has the most likes on TikTok as an individual creator her account has accumulated approximately 12.1 billion cumulative likes.

The record for the most liked single video, however, belongs to a different name entirely: Australian creator Leah Halton (@looooooooch), whose lip-sync post sits at around 74.4 million likes as of early 2026.

## Who Has the Most Likes on TikTok What Are We Actually Measuring?

When people look up who has the most likes on TikTok, they are typically asking one of two very different questions which account has accumulated the highest total likes across every video ever posted, or which single video has received the most individual likes.

These are two entirely separate records. Knowing the difference matters, because the answer changes completely depending on which one you mean.

At the account level, total likes represent a running sum of every reaction received across all uploaded content. Charli D'Amelio leads this ranking by a wide margin.

What often gets overlooked is that some of the most-liked TikTok accounts are not individual creators at all. Media brands like Barstool Sports and ESPN appear near the top of the leaderboard a direct result of their posting volume and massive existing audiences.

This mirrors a pattern visible across the wider creator economy, where high-frequency publishing accounts often match or exceed individual influencers in total engagement figures.

If you're curious how different apps and socials stack up in terms of engagement strategy, the gap between brand accounts and individual creators is a recurring theme across platforms.

## Top 10 Most-Liked TikTok Accounts in 2026

| Rank | Creator / Account | Total Likes | Followers | Account Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Charli D'Amelio | 12.1B | 157.8M | Individual |
| 2 | Barstool Sports | 9.9B | 49.2M | Brand/Media |
| 3 | Susma (anubhav) | 8.6B | 95.5K | Individual* |
| 4 | Domelipa | 5.3B | 75.8M | Individual |
| 5 | Addison Rae | 5.3B | 88.1M | Individual |
| 6 | ESPN | 5.2B | 57.7M | Brand/Media |
| 7 | Sisoy | 4.8B | 8.1M | Individual |
| 8 | Brooke Monk | 4.4B | 46.6M | Individual |
| 9 | Kimberly Loaiza | 4.3B | 83.8M | Individual |
| 10 | Pubity | 4.0B | 18.5M | Brand/Media |

Source: Social Blade, 2026. *Rank 3 flagged as a data anomaly — see note below.

One figure in this dataset stands out immediately and warrants caution. The account at rank 3 Susma (anubhav) shows 8.6 billion total likes against only 95,500 followers.

No ratio in organic TikTok engagement comes close to that. No explanation exists within the source data, and this figure should be treated with skepticism until independently verified.

Tools built around new software and data tracking are increasingly being used to flag exactly these kinds of anomalies in social media datasets.

## Charli D'Amelio — How She Became TikTok's Most-Liked Creator

Charli D'Amelio joined TikTok in 2019 and grew faster than virtually anyone else on the platform during its most explosive period.

She currently holds around 157.8 million followers and has posted over 3,100 videos both figures directly relevant to understanding how she reached 12.1 billion total likes.

According to data from Statista, Charli D'Amelio had already become the most-liked TikTok creator in the United States as early as July 2020, having accumulated 5.2 billion likes faster than any other creator on the platform at that time.

### The Factors Behind Her Extraordinary Like Count

Volume is the foundation. More than 3,000 uploaded videos means significantly more opportunities for likes to compound over time.

Her content primarily dance-based and trend-driven aligned precisely with what TikTok's algorithm was amplifying during the platform's highest-growth window between 2019 and 2022.

Early-mover advantage also played a decisive role.

As reported by TechCrunch, TikTok saw 325% growth in 2020, with monthly time spent per user increasing faster than any other app that year. Creators who were already active and posting consistently during that window accumulated engagement at a rate that has since proven very difficult to replicate.

Staying on top of the latest in tech shows just how rapidly platform dynamics shift, making timing on any social platform a critical variable for long-term growth.

Guinness World Records officially confirmed Charli D'Amelio as the most liked TikTok user (female category) with 11.5 billion likes, verified as of 19 February 2024.

Current tracking through Social Blade shows continued growth beyond that point. It is worth noting that GWR uses a gendered framing for this record a comparable male category is not currently addressed in available GWR public data.

## The Most Liked Individual TikTok Videos of 2026

This ranking operates on entirely different logic from account-level totals, and the two lists barely overlap. The creators behind the most-liked single videos are largely not the same people who dominate the account leaderboard.

As of early 2026, Leah Halton (@looooooooch) holds the record for the most liked TikTok video a lip-sync clip that has surpassed the record previously held for years by Bella Poarch.

| Rank | Creator Handle | Video Description | Likes | Year Posted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | @looooooooch | Lip-sync / summer trend video | 74.4M | 2024 |
| 2 | @bellapoarch | Lip-sync ("Build a B*tch" era) | 73.3M | 2020 |
| 3 | @thenickluciano | Comedy / reaction clip | 57.0M | 2021 |
| 4 | @jamie32bsh | Dance / music video clip | 54.4M | N/A |
| 5 | @franekbielak_art | Drawing / art reveal | 52.1M | 2021 |
| 6 | @pr4yforgabs | Food / aesthetic video | 51.8M | N/A |
| 7 | @mngnzls | Comedy / audio clip | 46.2M | N/A |
| 8 | @totouchanemu | Drone / outdoor video | 45.7M | N/A |
| 9 | @billieeilish | TimeWarpScan filter video | 43.1M | 2021 |
| 10 | @adrianchateau | Comedy reaction clip | 40.9M | N/A |

Source: RouteNote, updated February 2026.

Most of these videos went viral through a combination of well-timed posting, a catchy audio track, and the inherent unpredictability of TikTok's For You Page algorithm.

Notably, none of these creators appear anywhere in the top 10 most-liked accounts list which reveals something important about how single-video virality differs fundamentally from sustained account-level engagement.

Platforms that aggregate digital content trends, such as www.aeonscope.net, consistently show this same split between one-hit viral moments and long-term cumulative performance.

Also Read: Latest in Tech from Aliensync

## Why the Most Followed TikTok Creator Doesn't Have the Most Likes

This distinction surprises many people. Khabane Lame is TikTok's most-followed creator at 161.2 million followers slightly ahead of Charli D'Amelio but his total likes sit at approximately 2.6 billion, placing him at around rank 32 on the overall likes leaderboard.

That gap is striking. Charli's 12.1 billion likes is nearly five times Khabane's total, despite her having a marginally smaller audience.

### Why Follower Count and Like Count Tell Different Stories

Several factors explain this divergence.Khabane Lame built his following primarily through silent reaction videos a format that spreads efficiently and earns followers, but does not consistently generate the same like-to-view ratio as music-driven or trend-based content.

He has also posted fewer videos overall, approximately 1,320 compared to Charli's 3,100-plus.

Timing is the other major variable. Creators who were posting heavily during TikTok's 2019–2021 boom years benefited from an organic reach environment that no longer exists.

A video posted in 2020 with genuine momentum could accumulate likes continuously for years after posting.

In practical terms: follower count reflects visibility and reach. Total likes reflect consistent output, content format, and the era in which that content was produced. They measure related but meaningfully different things.

## Final Answer — Who Has the Most Likes on TikTok?

Charli D'Amelio leads TikTok in cumulative account likes at 12.1 billion. Leah Halton holds the record for the most liked single video at 74.4 million likes.

Neither title belongs to TikTok's most-followed creator, Khabane Lame a distinction that reveals how differently reach, virality, and sustained engagement actually work on the platform.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Who has the most likes on TikTok overall?

Charli D'Amelio holds the most cumulative likes on TikTok as an individual creator, with approximately 12.1 billion total likes across her account as of 2026.

### Who has the most likes on a single TikTok video?

Leah Halton (@looooooooch) holds the record for the most liked single TikTok video with approximately 74.4 million likes as of early 2026, overtaking the record Bella Poarch had held for several years.

### Does Khabane Lame have the most likes on TikTok?

No. Khabane Lame is TikTok's most-followed creator but ranks approximately 32nd in total account likes with around 2.6 billion well behind Charli D'Amelio's 12.1 billion.

### How does TikTok count likes per video or per account?

Both. Each video carries its own individual like count. An account's total likes figure is the combined sum of likes received across every video that account has ever posted.

### Has Charli D'Amelio's record been officially confirmed?

Yes. Guinness World Records verified Charli D'Amelio as the most liked TikTok user (female category) with 11.5 billion likes as of February 19, 2024. Current Social Blade tracking shows that figure has continued to grow since then.

# Bella Poarch’s viral “M to the B” TikTok breaks record for most likes

Published: Sep 12, 2020, 22:58

TikTok superstar Bella Poarch has officially earned the most likes on a TikTok video after cracking 30 million upvotes for bopping her head to Millie B’s “M to the B” track.

Charli D’Amelio and Michael ‘JustMaiko’ Le may have more followers than Bella Poarch, but her “M to the B” video has vastly exceeded the likes anyone has ever received for a TikTok video.

Poarch, a 19-year-old Filipina and U.S. Navy veteran who resides in Hawaii, uploaded her video on August 17. At the time of writing, it has 364.1 million views, 891.3 thousand comments, and, most importantly, a stunning 31.3 million likes.

For context, the second-highest number of likes any video has achieved is around 25 million, posted by JustMaiko.

### TikTok’s top-five most liked videos

1. Bella Poarch’s “M to the B,” 31.3 millions
2. JustMaiko’s escalator dancing, 25.5 million
3. Kison Kee’s milk slip, 23.5 million
4. The Rock and Kevin Hart’s best-friend check, 22.2 million
5. The Rock and Kevin Hart’s Christmas, 20.9 million

A variety of comments have levied attacks against the influencer, citing a lack of talent and expressing shock that such a simple video has so many views and likes.

While it may be surprising, that’s what the internet is. Many more appreciate the video than hate on it, citing Poarch’s good vibes and calling the energy “satisfying.” Further, a look at everyone else who has used the sound proves why the content creator’s rendition is on a different level.

Originally, “M to the B” was a video that went viral in niche communities, following a Noisey documentary, for being an entertaining look into the drama within the Blackpool grime scene.

A sound using an iconic part of the song was posted on TikTok back in June and received millions of views. But it had no lasting power until Poarch coupled her look, which fans and peers describe as “cute” and “adorable,” with the unique track.

The shy, soft-spoken TikTok star Bella Poarch catapulted to fame by her hypnotizing head-bobbing video, which she uploaded on Aug. 17, 2020.

In the video, she is lip synching to M to the B by Millie B, complete with her animated facial expressions, and a Band-Aid on her chin. She used the app’s Face Zoom lens that gave the movement of her face a bouncy effect.

One year after the video was released, it’s still racking up likes, now at almost 52 million, and has been viewed for over 630 million times.

To celebrate the milestone of the life-changing feat, Bella indulged her fans with a TikTok duet of the original viral video. She nailed it, of course, sans the Face Zoom effect.

##duet with @bellapoarch 1 year ago today!? Bee yourself & don’t care what other people think & try new things. Thank you guys for changing my life.

> ♬ M to the B - Millie B

In the caption, she penned a message for her fans who are instrumental in achieving her success.

“1 year ago today! Bee yourself, and don’t care what other people think, and try new things. Thank you guys for changing my life,” Bella wrote.

Fans expressed their amusement that it has already been a year since the iconic video was uploaded. Even TikTok’s official account congratulated her and commented, “YES Bella! (Omg, it’s already been a year!?)”

In a recent H3 Podcast interview, Bella revealed that it took her two hours to perfect, with about a hundred drafts before settling on the now-iconic clip. She said upon the first day of posting, she got one million likes but believed it will slow down eventually, but it did not as the video is still gaining likes and views to this day.

To the ? ? ?#fyp

> ♬ M to the B - Millie B

Bella Poarch is currently the fourth most followed person on TikTok with 78 million followers, trailing behind Charli D’Amelio with over 122 million, Khaby Lame with 102 million, and Addison Rae with 82.5 million.

Bella’s TikTok account has almost two billion likes as of this writing.

Following her success in doing lip-synching videos, she slowly incorporates her love for music in her posts, where she sings, plays the ukulele and more. After all, music is her first love, according to her H3 interview.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bella Poarch (@bellapoarch)

Beyond her TikTok career, 24-year-old Bella released a single Build a Bitch in April 2021, which both song and video were well-received by fans.

She also recently released a song with Sub Urban titled Inferno, with a music video that featured cameos of social media personalities like Bretman Rock and Ivana Alawi.

Before gaining popularity on social media, Bella served in the US Navy for four years. She was born in the Philippines and moved to the US when she was 14 years old.
